notes: Product: VS Code extension for professional dev teams (inline suggestions, streaming completions)
Primary ask: sub-100ms median for single-line inline completions and streaming partial tokens to UI
CTO quote: 'If inline feels laggy our churn goes up — we need it indistinguishable from local completions'
Auth: prefer enterprise SSO (SAML) for org installs; also want scoped install tokens for CI/bot users
Rate limits: want per-install and per-user buckets, plus a burst allowance for live coding sessions — uncertain how Redwood's rate-limit headers map to editor UX
Model/versioning: require ability to pin per-workspace and a fast rollback (canary -> full) for breaking changes
Fallbacks: explicit preference to fallback from a high-cost, high-quality model to a low-latency quantized variant when latency SLOs breached
Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay for predictable latency; will optimize with Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, cache) if available
Data residency: dev teams spread NA/EU, prefer routing to nearest region and option to keep telemetry in-customer VPC for enterprise customers
UI/SDK: needs streaming SSE and websockets for incremental tokens; extension uses small buffers and needs partial token commit API to avoid flicker
Observability: require per-token cost breakdown in console, traces correlated to editor session IDs
POC constraints: will run 2-week PoC with 2k daily active editors, peak concurrency 400, test harness stored in Drive link
Jira: RDW-3421 tracks auth spec gaps; RDW-3499 tracks rate-limit behavior observed in lab run
Decision factors: latency (primary), predictable billing (secondary), and clean auth model for org installs
